text:
ash: CI perf alert on PR #13075 — microbench warmstart timer increased by +14% vs golden, failing threshold. link: https://ci.redwood.example/runs/13075/artifacts :eyes:
ash: Repro locally? I ran `./tools/bench/run --micro micro_warmstart --model rwd-7b --seed 42` and saw similar jump on batcher path
lina: Pinging CI logs. Which metric exactly? tail-latency P95 or avg tokens/sec?
ash: P95 tokens/sec dropped. Golden: 520 tok/s, PR: 450 tok/s on the same machine type. Also saw longer kernel selection time in the profiler.
jamie: CI bot output: `microbench: warmstart_timer=0.012 -> 0.014(s) kernel_select_ms=1.8 -> 3.1` (threshold delta 20%) — pasted from artifact.
ci-bot: Build #13075 — perf-check failed: threshold_delta=+14% (P95 tokens/sec). Artifacts: flamegraph.svg, perf_hist.json, kernel-chooser.log
mateo: Can someone share the flamegraph link? I'll check whether kernel selector syscall increased.
ash: flamegraph: https://ci.redwood.example/artifacts/13075/flamegraph.svg — top hotspot is `KernelScheduler::choose_best` during warmstart loop.
lina: Hmm, recent commits in the PR changed scheduler weighting: commit c3f2d9b updated `seqlen_affinity` scoring to prefer small kernels. Could that cause oscillation on warmstart? :thinking_face:
jamie: If kernel chooser now probes more candidates, that adds overhead at cold/warm starts. We intentionally added a fallback probe to avoid bad long kernels, but it might be too eager.
mateo: Quick check: git blame shows c3f2d9b added a `for` loop over candidates; before we limited to top-1. New code:
```
for (auto& cand : candidates) {
  score = score_candidate(cand);
  if (score > best + kProbeMargin) { best = score; }
}
```
That will evaluate multiple kernels instead of returning early.
ash: Repro snippet that shows overhead:
```
$ perf record -g -- ./bin/runtime --test-warmstart
perf report: samples in KernelScheduler::choose_best increased 1.7x
```
lina: Can we reproduce on CI machine image with same seed and compare `--kernel-autoselect=false`?
jamie: I toggled `--kernel-autoselect=false` locally; tokens/sec returned to 515, within golden noise. So autoselect path is the culprit.
mateo: Good isolate. Do we have a unit test for kernel chooser budget? I recall a microbench that checks chooser latency, but threshold is loose.
nash: There is `bench/kernel_selector_latency` but it only asserts <5ms; our change pushed it to ~6ms in worst-case. We need to tighten or adjust logic.
lina: Given this is a PR blocking perf gate, options: revert commit c3f2d9b, or apply a quick hotfix: short-circuit the loop when best exceeds (kBestMargin) to avoid scanning all candidates.
jamie: I can open a follow-up PR with early-return and a unit test. Quick revert would be faster for rollout. What do we want for the branch?
mateo: If we revert, we should also add a canary test to CI to catch selector scan cost. If we hotfix, add the test too.
nash: CI: any chance this only happens on specific GPU HW? The failing runner was `g4dn-xlarge-rt` type. I repro on local `g4dn` shape. Might be common.
ci-bot: Note: PR #13060 (merged recently) touched scheduler heuristics too — might interact. Recommend bisect across these two PRs.
lina: I'll start a bisect job across merges between build 4476920000..4477000000.
nash: Meanwhile, jamie, please draft the revert PR so we can land ASAP if bisect implicates c3f2d9b. Add benchmark artifact to PR.
jamie: On it. Draft: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/13102 — includes revert plus added microbench assertion.
```
- revert c3f2d9b
- add test bench/kernel_selector_latency with --repeat 20
```
mateo: Also adding an integration check to CI that runs `bench/micro_warmstart` under `--kernel-autoselect` on a small subset to catch regressions.
nash: After revert landed locally, I ran the microbench on the same CI image: P95 tokens/sec back to 522. Good.
jamie: Submitted PR 13102, requested reviews from @lina @ash. :hammer_and_wrench:
lina: Reviewed and approved. Merged.
ci-bot: PR 13102 merged; triggering perf job for affected runs.
ci-bot: Perf job results: threshold_delta now -1.2% (within noise). Tests green.
nash: Thanks everyone. Followups: (1) add more conservative probe budget to kernel chooser, (2) add unit test for probe count, (3) mark scheduler heuristics PR 13060 for additional review for interactions.
mateo: I'll file a ticket with profiling screenshots and a proposed change to kProbeMargin.
jamie: I'll own the probe-budget patch and CI test.
lina: Great triage. Closing this thread once tickets are up. :white_check_mark:
